title: Canonicalize finite-field trace phases with Frobenius orbits
summary: Provides canonical simplification for Boolean trace functions, additive-character sums, coding constructions, and comparison of finite-field phase representations.
content: For Tr_F(2^N)/F2(f(x)), rotate positive exponents by doubling modulo 2^N-1, move coefficients by the matching Frobenius power, and combine each orbit. Short orbits require a relative trace followed by a trace-one lift back to the ambient field. Positive multiples of 2^N-1 must not be replaced by exponent zero. For Boolean cubics, the sharp maximum least exponent among the relevant necklaces is 1+2^floor(N/3)+2^floor(2N/3).
whenToUse: Provides canonical simplification for Boolean trace functions, additive-character sums, coding constructions, and comparison of finite-field phase representations.
limitations: Equality is of traces on the chosen field, not geometric equivalence of curves or equality on all extension fields. The degree bound is still exponential and does not imply hardness. The current BinaryField helper enumerates small fields for verification; a scalable implementation must use polynomial-time field/linear-algebra routines described in the notes.
